$description: Struct-level golden vectors for canonicalBoxBytes — the box identity encoding that computeBoxId and computeTxId hash (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Layout - Boxes). A positional layout. One vector per box type, because the per-type field lists are separate layouts sharing a two-field prefix — plus a second genesis_proof vector, because an empty payload is what its length prefix exists for, and a second emission vector at zero, because that is where the format's two-byte floor is, and a second fee vector at zero, because that is a shape the encoder must write and the ledger never holds, and a second karma_pool vector at zero, because that zero is one the ledger DOES hold. Two groups are deliberate: invite and bond share identical trailing fields, and emission, treasury, fee and karma_pool share the absence of any, so in both the tag byte is the whole of what separates their leaves.

vectors.name: box/karma-minimal
vectors.note: 35 bytes, and every one of them is a field the layout table names: one tag byte, one value byte, the 32-byte owner, and the absent decayBurn option's 00. No key names — the field list is positional, so it costs nothing in the bytes. This is the smallest a karma box gets.

vectors.name: box/karma-decay-burn
vectors.note: The karma arm's option present: `01` is the present tag and the second `01` is the boolean, two bytes where box/karma-minimal spends one. decayBurn is what gates the decay clock, so this is the one vector that pins the encoding of a field production reads rather than merely stores. The all-ff owner also keeps the option bytes visible against a field that is not all-ff.

vectors.name: box/karma-value-u64-max
vectors.note: The whole argument for the bigint exception, in one vector: those ten bytes are the all-ones sentinel a malformed NUMBER field takes, and here they are a perfectly legal box value. `value: bigint` spans the entire u64, so no sentinel is unreachable and its writer has to throw instead — sentinelling would give a malformed box a well-formed box's id.

vectors.name: box/credit-transfer-sentinel
vectors.note: The smallest credit box: value 1, the owner, and the absent lockedUntilBlock option. 35 bytes, the same width as box/karma-minimal — the two arms differ only in the tag byte and in which writer the option wraps, so the enum8 tag is the whole of what separates them here.

vectors.name: box/credit-wide
vectors.note: value > 2^53 — the range a `number` cannot hold, which is why box values are bigint at all. Eight VLQ bytes here; box/karma-value-u64-max carries the ten-byte maximum. lockedUntilBlock 720 is present, so the option's other branch is covered on this type and it takes vlqU past one byte: 720 is d0 05.

vectors.name: box/invite
vectors.note: An invite always holds 0 — the karma it names is minted at the claim, not carried here — so the value byte is 00 and the whole tail is two adjacent b32 fields. Read against box/bond below: the trailing layouts are identical, so a swap of inviterId and inviteePublicKey shows up here rather than as a moved id much later, and the tag byte is the whole of what separates the two types.

vectors.name: box/genesis-proof-typical
vectors.note: The only arm whose whole tail is one lp field, and the only type whose value is fixed at 0 — the box holds neither karma nor credits, so it never enters supply accounting. `0d` is the payload's length prefix: the field is lp and not lpUtf8 because the bytes are opaque to consensus, so a conformance reader must not attempt UTF-8 on them. Production content is the per-network NetworkProfile.genesisProofPayload; this vector's is its own.

vectors.name: box/genesis-proof-empty-payload
vectors.note: Three bytes — the smallest box that carries a tail, and the case that pins why the payload is length-prefixed. Appended raw, an empty payload would be indistinguishable from the end of the box, and a one-byte payload of 00 would encode as 030000 too. Here the trailing 00 is the count, and a one-byte payload of 00 is 03000100. box/emission-zero reaches two by carrying no tail at all.

vectors.name: box/bond
vectors.note: The same two trailing fields as box/invite under tag 04, so this pair is one layout with two tags and enum8(boxType) is field 1 for exactly that reason. 66 bytes. A bond is byte-identical from creation to the block that consumes it: the invitee key names the paired invite by itself, and no probation field is carried because the window is dated from IdentityRecord.invitedAtBlock.

vectors.name: box/post-lock
vectors.note: The lock's target is NOT in the box. A post id comes from the transaction that creates the lock, so a targetPostId field would have to be known before the TxId that produces it — unbuildable. Node derives the mapping at apply. originalValue is vlqU64 (bigint, throwing) and precedes owner.

vectors.name: box/vouch
vectors.note: Value is always 1 karma on this type, so the vector's job is the two identity fields and the tag.

vectors.name: box/emission
vectors.note: The first box type whose whole encoding is the shared prefix - tag byte, value, and nothing after it. There is no owner because block application is the only spender. The value is mainnet's entire emission total, 422,640,000 credits at 8 decimals, which is what genesis puts in the box; eight VLQ bytes carry it, so the whole box is nine. Read against box/treasury below: with no trailing fields at all, the tag byte is the whole of what separates the empty-tail types.

vectors.name: box/treasury
vectors.note: Byte-for-byte box/emission under tag 08, deliberately at the same value: the empty layout carries three tags - emission, treasury and fee - the same standing box/invite and box/bond have with two shared fields, and this pair is where the corpus holds it at equal value. Their ids part on the provenance computeBoxId appends, never on these bytes. A treasury box never actually holds the emission total - the value is chosen to make the collision case the vector, not to describe a reachable state.

vectors.name: box/emission-zero
vectors.note: Two bytes - the smallest legal box of any type, and the floor for the whole format. Every other arm carries a tail: box/genesis-proof-empty-payload is three because its empty payload still spends a length prefix. The value is 0 for the byte width alone; block application creates no successor at zero, so this is a shape the encoder must handle and the ledger never holds.

vectors.name: box/fee
vectors.note: What a credit transaction pays for its inclusion, named as an output so the transaction balances exactly. The third type whose whole encoding is the shared prefix, under tag 09: no owner, because block application is the only spender and the coinbase already decides which key the fee reaches. 1000000 base units is 0.01 credits and takes three VLQ bytes - c0 84 3d, the low group first - so the value's multi-byte form is covered on an empty-tail arm as well as on box/emission.

vectors.name: box/fee-zero
vectors.note: Two bytes, box/emission-zero under the other tag. A zero-value fee box is one consensus never creates - zero fee means no box - and it still ENCODES: the no-zero rule belongs to block application, not to this encoder, whose domain on value is the whole u64. That split is the same one an over-bound genesis_proof payload has, one direction over.

vectors.name: box/karma-pool-genesis
vectors.note: The whole of a network's karma supply as genesis holds it: the maximum representable karma, under tag 0a, with nothing after the prefix. Eleven bytes, ten of them the value - the top of vlqU64's range, and the same ten bytes box/karma-value-u64-max carries ahead of a 33-byte tail. pool.value + circulating karma == 2^64 - 1 at every height, so this is the ceiling the box can hold and the writer is never handed one past it. Genesis committee grants are drawn out of this total rather than minted beside it.

vectors.name: box/karma-pool-zero
vectors.note: Two bytes, box/emission-zero under tag 0a - and the reason inverts. Emission terminates, so no zero successor is created and box/emission-zero is a shape the ledger never holds; the pool never terminates, because a burn must always have somewhere to return, so the box exists at every height whatever its value. This is the one empty-tail zero that is a reachable state rather than an encoder shape, which is exactly what a reader pattern-matching to the emission rule gets backwards.

rejects.name: box/genesis-proof-payload-over-bound
rejects.note: A 513-byte payload, one past MAX_GENESIS_PROOF_PAYLOAD_BYTES. Every byte of it is present and the lp field is well formed, so nothing here is truncated and nothing re-encodes differently - the bound is the only rule that can refuse these bytes, and 8104 is the count that makes them 513 rather than 512. The bound is per-type and lives in the genesis_proof arm of the reader, never in readLp, which every lp field shares; box/genesis-proof-typical is the same layout inside the bound. An over-bound payload still ENCODES, exactly as an unknown boxType does - the writers are total and the refusal is one-way.

rejects.name: box/unassigned-tag-11
rejects.note: 11 is the first tag the table does not assign, and an unassigned tag has no decoding at all — the reader refuses it rather than skipping to the next field. Distinct from box/unknown-tag-255 below: 0xff is the sentinel an unknown boxType WRITES, while this is simply a number nothing claims, and both must be one-way. The number here is load-bearing and STAYS LITERAL: a corpus deriving its input from the code under test checks nothing, so a tag this vector names is one the table must not claim, and assigning it is what moves this vector. packages/types/test/utxo.test.ts derives the same number from BOX_TYPE_TAGS, which is the other half of the pair - one side follows the table, one side pins it.

rejects.name: box/unknown-tag-255
rejects.note: 0xff is what enum8 WRITES for an unknown boxType, and it must not decode back into anything. That one-wayness is why the tag writer can stay total where the fixed-width writers cannot: a malformed box encodes, but never as a valid one.

rejects.name: box/non-minimal-value
rejects.note: box/karma-minimal with `value` padded from 64 to e4 00. It decodes to 100 either way — only the re-encode compare rejects it, and this is the field a malleability attempt would target because it is what a box is worth.

rejects.name: box/trailing-byte
rejects.note: box/karma-minimal plus a byte. Appended junk is a rejection, not slack — the defect class this format exists to close is junk riding inside a committed structure.

rejects.name: box/bond-short-invitee-key
rejects.note: box/bond with 31 bytes of invitee key instead of 32. The field is b32, so an off-domain width has no encoding at all rather than sharing one with a valid bond — the writer throws and the reader runs out of bytes. Its domain is established upstream, by node's output-shape schema.

rejects.name: box/karma-decay-burn-not-a-boolean
rejects.note: The karma option's PRESENT branch carrying 0xff where the boolean goes. `writeBool`'s domain is {0,1} inside a byte, so the other 254 have no encoding and the reader refuses them rather than reading any non-zero as true — a lenient reader would map 254 byte strings onto one value, and every one of them would re-encode to 01.
